answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering: score each identity by its long-run distribution of action types and compare against the co-occurrence patterns seen across a seasoned voyage of organic accounts. When a cluster of new identities shows suspiciously similar fingerprints, enforcement retroactively merges them and reallocates rewards, treating each as one island of influence rather than many. An attacker must then fund real, divergent behavior across every sock puppet, and that saffron-thin margin of uniqueness costs them sustained compute and weeks of genuine interaction per identity.
